claim: FileDiscovery is described by its author as 'the first EndpointDiscovery backend for non-Kubernetes deployments' in llm-d-router: it reads a YAML or JSON file listing inference endpoints and drives their lifecycle in the router's datastore via a DiscoveryNotifier.
stance_target: llm-d-router now ships a concrete, non-Kubernetes-native discovery backend implementation
quoted_support: This PR implements the FileDiscovery plugin, the first EndpointDiscovery backend for non-Kubernetes deployments. It reads a YAML or JSON file that lists inference endpoints and drives their lifecycle in the datastore via DiscoveryNotifier.

claim: FileDiscovery supports zero-downtime endpoint updates by optionally watching its backing file with fsnotify, reconciling endpoint additions and removals on every write, and diffing the previous snapshot against new file contents to remove stale endpoints on reload.
stance_target: operational mechanics for updating a non-k8s backend's endpoint set at runtime
quoted_support: Optionally watches the file with fsnotify and reconciles additions/removals on every write, allowing zero-downtime endpoint updates without restarting the EPP. Removes stale endpoints on reload by diffing the previous snapshot against the new file contents.

claim: FileDiscovery is configured via EndpointPickerConfig.dataLayer.discovery.pluginRef, referencing a plugin instance of type 'file-discovery' with 'path' and 'watchFile' parameters; as merged in PR #1135 the plugin was implemented and unit-tested in isolation but not yet wired into the runner, so setting this config had no effect until the follow-on PR #1218 (4/4) shipped.
stance_target: exact config surface and the precise point at which file-discovery became actually usable end-to-end
quoted_support: The FileDiscovery plugin is fully implemented and tested in isolation but is not yet usable end-to-end. The runner wiring plugin registration, config detection, and the runWithFileDiscovery execution path will land in the next (and final) PR. Until then setting dataLayer.discovery.pluginRef in the config will have no effect.

claim: During code review, a per-endpoint metrics-port override field (MetricsHost, later MetricsPort) was proposed and then entirely dropped because 'the EPP can not scrape and serve on different IPs, only same IP and different port is feasible (and deprecated)'; the shipped FileDiscovery plugin always scrapes Prometheus metrics from the same address:port the endpoint serves inference traffic on, with no configurable separate metrics endpoint.
stance_target: concrete constraint on backend heterogeneity: non-k8s endpoints registered via file-discovery must expose metrics on the same host:port as inference traffic
quoted_support: sounds like only a port change makes sense. The EPP can not scrape and serve on different IPs, only same IP and different port is feasible (and deprecated). ... as you suggested I removed the MetricsPort and HOST completely so scrapping always from address:port

claim: The FileDiscovery plugin validates and accepts only IPv4 endpoint addresses, explicitly rejecting IPv6 addresses.
stance_target: concrete limitation for non-k8s backend addressing via file-discovery
quoted_support: file-discovery: validate IPv4 only and reject IPv6 addresses

claim: Despite being the non-Kubernetes discovery backend, FileDiscovery's internal endpoint-identity tracking still uses Kubernetes' types.NamespacedName as the map key type for tracking known endpoints, confirming the k8s-shaped identifier gap flagged as unresolved in the earlier discovery-interface PR (#908) persisted into the file-based implementation.
stance_target: the file-discovery implementation is fully decoupled from Kubernetes-specific types
quoted_support: endpoints map[types.NamespacedName]struct{} ... // from the last successful load. Used as a key set only -- values are zero-byte structs. Compared against the entries parsed during a reload to compute which endpoints to delete from the datastore.

claim: A fix during review re-attaches the fsnotify watcher after atomic file renames and Kubernetes ConfigMap rotation, indicating the FileDiscovery plugin was explicitly designed to also work when its backing file is mounted into a Kubernetes pod from a ConfigMap (which updates via atomic symlink swap), not only for fully non-Kubernetes deployments.
stance_target: file-discovery is usable both fully outside Kubernetes and as an alternative discovery mechanism inside a Kubernetes pod
quoted_support: re-attach fsnotify watcher after atomic rename and ConfigMap rotation

claim: File-based discovery is described by its author as 'the first phase in re-creating the functionality of' an earlier closed PR (#1007, 'Discovery Plugins: K8s and File-based Endpoint Discovery'), and the plugin was hardened during review to 'skip invalid endpoints on reload instead of aborting the entire load' and to fix a partial-Upsert atomicity bug that could leave zombie endpoints in the datastore.
stance_target: provenance and reliability hardening of the file-discovery implementation
quoted_support: The file based discovery is the first phase in re-creating the functionality of #1007. ... a partial-Upsert atomicity bug that can leave zombie endpoints in the datastore; and missing watcher re-add that breaks watchFile mode after atomic renames
